methods.spectral_method: One-sided Hann-window PSD averaged over 50%-overlapping windows plus final endpoint. FFT size min(131072, largest power of two within clip). Channels averaged after power, preserving anti-phase energy.
methods.display: 160 logarithmic bands from 20 Hz to 22050 Hz. power_share is integrated energy per band divided by total in that range; relative_db uses the strongest displayed energy band as 0 dB. Unequal band widths mean this is band energy, not power density.
methods.dominant_tone: Interpolated strongest peak in the full-clip Hann spectrum above 20 Hz. Suitable as a tone estimate for known synthetic stimuli, not a general fundamental or binaural-beat detector.
methods.levels: RMS and peak are digital dBFS, not calibrated loudness at the ear. No waveform normalization precedes measurements.
methods.ratings: Provided aggregate perceived-valence/arousal means on 1–5 scales. SDs are rounded source SDs. Forty annotators in the study; per-stimulus n is not provided. No individual ratings are redistributed.
methods.release_difference: The 2018 paper and landing-page prose describe 144 stimuli. The corrected Zenodo archive analyzed here contains 168 WAVs and 168 matching rating rows: 14 frequency indices × 3 waveforms × 2 envelope codes × 2 duration codes.
methods.birdsong_interval: Only 60–90 seconds of each source is measured. The randomized study exposed participants to six minutes; an excerpt is not a tested intervention in itself.

rating_scale.arousal: Low = low arousal; high = high arousal

collections.label: Birdsong / traffic · randomized study stimuli
collections.license: No license assigned in OSF metadata; raw recordings are not redistributed
collections.evidence: Exact stimuli from a six-minute randomized study of anxiety and related outcomes; no per-clip comfort ratings or migraine claim

emosynth.interpretation: Descriptive associations within this synthetic collection only. Means give each stimulus equal weight; stimulus-level rating counts are unavailable. Related parameter combinations are not independent participants. No p-values, treatment effect, or optimum are inferred.
